thread:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 latency spike detected for eu-west-2 streaming path (autodetect). Trigger: p99 > 5s for 3m, increased error rate on streaming sockets. https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/r/streaming?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-2 :rotating_light:
ivy_sre: saw it — p95 jumped from ~450ms to ~2.2s, p99 ~6.7s. Stream stall traces show long TLS handshake times and SYN retries.
ryan_net: interesting — any cross-zone routing changes in the last hour? I don't see infra deploys but there was a routing flapping notice from cloud provider at 3376543000.
maya_prod: customer-facing: one enterprise account reported intermittent partial responses and websocket disconnects starting ~10:50 UTC. Support ticket #CS-8421 opened.
alex_support: confirmed, CS escalated to SE. They see repeated reconnect attempts and truncated outputs. Ticket contains user-side traceroute showing high RTT to nat-01-eu-west2.
ivy_sre: initial hypothesis: NAT egress path for eu-west-2 overloaded, causing ephemeral port exhaustion and TLS handshake tail latency. Packet drops upstream would explain retransmits + SLO breaching.
ryan_net: grabbing tcpdump on a few affected nodes now. If NAT device is dropping, we should see SYN retransmits and RSTs. Running `sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0'` on proxy hosts.
ivy_sre: also started collecting streaming gateway logs and kv-cache hit rates to rule out backend stalls.
ryan_net: quick check: `ss -s` shows high TCP established count and a lot of sockets in TIME_WAIT on nat-proxy-03. Ephemeral port usage at 96%.
ivy_sre: that's consistent. If ephemeral ports exhausted, new TLS handshakes will queue and stall (p99 shoots up).
ryan_net: suggest immediate mitigation: rotate NAT gateway / enable additional NAT pool in eu-west-2 to relieve SNAT consumption. I can trigger failover to nat-standby-2. Need oncall approval to modify egress config.
maya_prod: approve. We need to avoid config churn that impacts other regions. Plan: add extra SNAT IPs to node pool, then gradually drain nat-proxy-03.
oncall-bot: @ivy_sre you are oncall. Handoff in 8m to @ryan_net for network ops.
ivy_sre: I'm staying until handoff. Ryan — please coordinate with infra to add 32 additional SNAT addresses and bump conntrack. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/nat-ephemeral-ports. Steps I'm executing now: 1) increase conntrack max on proxies; 2) add SNAT IPs; 3) monitor p99.
ryan_net: starting step 2 now, opening change with infra: `change: add-snat-32-eu-west2` referencing CL-5402.
alex_support: posted status update to customer and CS channel: "We're investigating increased latency and reconnects in EU region; mitigation in progress." :white_check_mark:
ivy_sre: conntrack tuned (`sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000`) on nat-proxy-01/02/03. After tune we should see fewer drop-induced retransmits.
ryan_net: infra added the 32 SNAT IPs to the elastic pool. Confirmed on control plane that nat-01-eu-west2 has 32 extra translations available.
ivy_sre: monitoring shows ephemeral usage drop from 96% -> 42% over 60s. p95 trending down to ~600ms, p99 still ~2.1s. 
maya_prod: partial recovery noted, but still seeing streaming stalls for a subset of clients pinned to nat-proxy-03.
ryan_net: starting graceful drain of nat-proxy-03 (marking host as unsched for new connections) and bumping BGP weight on nat-standby-2 to attract traffic.
ivy_sre: useful logs from streaming gateway: ```
[2026-03-15T10:53:21Z] stream_conn: handshake_time=6721ms remote_ip=10.4.5.87 route=natted
[2026-03-15T10:53:22Z] stream_conn: handshake_time=12ms remote_ip=10.4.6.12 route=direct
```
ivy_sre: note disparity — some routes fine, others very slow. Strongly points at path-level egress problem.
ryan_net: after drain started, SYN retransmit rate decreased by 80% on nat-proxy-03. p99 dropped to ~1.3s within 90s.
alex_support: updated customer: "We've added capacity and are draining the problematic egress node; you should see stable connections within a few minutes."
ivy_sre: we'll keep running KV cache warmers and keep an eye on streaming stalls. If p99 doesn't go below 800ms within 10m, escalate to infrastructure paging.
ryan_net: also checking DNS resolver timeouts — cloud provider resolver had increased latency concurrent with the incident. Some clients used provider DNS for egress targets, causing chained delays.
maya_prod: adding follow-up item: improve egress observability — label per-connection NAT allocation and expose ephemeral utilization metric in console.
ivy_sre: agreed. Short-term follow-ups: 1) add SNAT pool autoscaling, 2) increase conntrack headroom, 3) alert on ephemeral > 75%. Long-term: route diversity and per-az NAT pools to avoid single-host exhaustion.
oncall-bot: Handoff: @ryan_net will take primary for the next hour. Paging schedule adjusted.
ryan_net: I'll stay on for 60m, will coordinate postmortem draft. Can someone capture the timeline and affected customer list?
alex_support: capturing — affected: EU streaming customers with persistent websocket connections started 2026-03-15T10:50:00Z. Primary impacted ASNs: 32934, 16509 (sample). Ticket numbers: CS-8421, CS-8422.
ivy_sre: metrics snapshot for postmortem: p95 pre-incident 0.45s, peak p95 2.2s, p99 pre 1.1s, peak p99 6.7s, error rate spike +2.4%. Throttle reasons: conntrack drops and NAT ephemeral exhaustion.
ryan_net: I'll add network-side graphs and tcpdump snippets to the incident doc. For remediation timeline: 10:52 — detect, 10:54 — conntrack bump, 10:56 — add SNAT IPs, 10:58 — begin drain, 11:00 — p99 below 2s, 11:05 — p99 ~1.1s, 11:10 — stable.
maya_prod: good, we can close pages once p99 holds <800ms for 30m and no new customer reports.
ivy_sre: filing incident with severity S2 -> S3 downgrade once stable. Will prepare action items for next oncall sync.
ryan_net: one more note — noted packet loss on provider uplink to azb at the same time window; filing a ticket with provider. Trace ID: prov-3376543-uplink.
alex_support: final status update posted to customers and CS.
ivy_sre: thanks everyone. I'll start the postmortem draft and include mitigation steps + pager tweaks. :memo:
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged, status: mitigated -> monitoring. If p99 regresses, incident will re-open
